| [QUESTION-245](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-245.md) | For linear decisions at the population level, if a kind's admissible transformations are given as a distribution over pairs of its realizations, is the top eigenspace of the pair operator a stable, decision-sufficient span, and what span takes that role when the pairs are directed? | The linear part of [QUESTION-052](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-052.md), split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md). Other spans can tie. Nonlinear decisions, and what picks one signature out, stay with [QUESTION-052](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-052.md). | Answered |
| [QUESTION-246](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-246.md) | In quantum theory, what does a failure of Kochen–Specker noncontextuality refute, as against a failure of Spekkens's generalized noncontextuality, and which of the two notions is broader? | The conceptual part of [QUESTION-067](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-067.md), split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) and answered by [THEORY-011](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-011.md), [THEORY-015](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-015.md), [THEORY-016](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-016.md), [THEORY-231](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-231.md) and [THEORY-559](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-559.md). | [QUESTION-247](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-247.md) v2 | If the communicative object is a presheaf of propositions over a category of contexts, is the negation its topos logic gives an orthocomplement or a Heyting pseudo-complement, and what fixes it? | The conditional part of [QUESTION-055](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-055.md), split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) and answered by [THEORY-516](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-516.md) and [THEORY-037](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-037.md). | [QUESTION-248](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-248.md) | In a stable linear Gaussian VAR(1), does a scalar linear coarse variable whose reduced dynamics carry memory admit an exact finite-dimensional Markovian augmentation? | [QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md) for the linear Gaussian class, split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) and answered by [CLAIM-398](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-398.md). | [QUESTION-272](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-272.md) v2 | When the task's target and the probes' outcome laws are both linear in one unknown state, as for the pairwise comparisons of actions under partial monitoring and for the authority shares of a mixture of known response profiles, when does a family of probes separate what the task needs told apart? | The part of [QUESTION-031](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-031.md) that the readings of 2026-10-25 settle, split off under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md). | [QUESTION-286](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-286.md) | Under smooth invertible changes of the parameter coordinates, which first-order frustration diagnoses among a learner's demands are invariant: pairwise Euclidean gradient angles, common strict first-order descent, or budgeted feasibility with the update geometry transported? | The coordinate part of [QUESTION-127](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-127.md), split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [CLAIM-366](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-366.md) (Active) settles it in full. | [QUESTION-287](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-287.md) | In a deterministic singularly perturbed system whose eliminated variable is fast and contracting and whose reduced system is contracting, does the memoryless quasi-steady-state reduction predict the coarse variable with an error bounded uniformly in time in terms of the eliminated dynamics? | The fast contracting case of [QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md), split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [THEORY-773](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-773.md) (Active) settles it. | [QUESTION-288](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-288.md) | Can preserving an inquiry's justificatory history improve decisions beyond a current state that is sufficient for those decisions, and can such a state stop being sufficient when a source, the model or the decision family changes? | A8's closing question, the part of [QUESTION-112](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-112.md) that A10 answered, split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [CLAIM-300](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-300.md) (Active) settles it in full. | [QUESTION-289](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-289.md) | Is an inquiry's current set of conclusions, or its logically closed belief set, enough to retain to fix its future revisions, and if not, what must a single AGM change of a closed theory have besides the theory? | The lower edge of [QUESTION-105](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-105.md), split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [CLAIM-294](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-294.md), [THEORY-347](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-347.md) and [THEORY-353](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-353.md) (all Active) settle it. No: two histories can agree on every current conclusion and call for different revisions, and two bases with one closure can revise to opposite conclusions. | [QUESTION-291](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-291.md) | For finite X and Y, does every finite-budget information-bottleneck optimum nest under the β → ∞ optimum, what test on a pair of optimal encoders decides whether two finite budgets nest, and do the optima nest at every pair of budgets when Y is a function of X or when X and Y are both binary? | The settled part of [QUESTION-220](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-220.md), split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [THEORY-743](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-743.md), [THEORY-753](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-753.md) and [THEORY-757](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-757.md) (Active) answer it. Every finite-β optimum is a stochastic coarsening of the causal partition. Two budgets nest iff some pair of optimal encoders forms X → T₂ → T₁, a convex-hull test on decoder points. The optima nest at every pair of budgets when Y is a function of X and when X and Y are both binary. | Answered |
| [QUESTION-292](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-292.md) | What evidence would show that a maintaining link, and not a regime's content, keeps a disorder in place: does the efficacy of a treatment that targets the link count, or only change in the link that is specific and comes before the outcome? | The evidential part of [QUESTION-045](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-045.md), split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [THEORY-053](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-053.md) (Active) settles it. A treatment's efficacy is not evidence for its theory of change. Only change in the theorised process that is specific and comes before the outcome bears on it, and moving the process without moving the outcome counts against the theory. | Answered |
| [QUESTION-293](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-293.md) | Is the distortion of a composite of approximate transports bounded by the sum of its parts' distortions, and does that additive bound survive when the distortion lacks a triangle inequality or a later kernel stretches distances? | The additive part of [QUESTION-017](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-017.md), split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [CLAIM-260](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-260.md) (Active) settles it in full. The composite of an ε₁-transport and an ε₂-transport is an (Lε₁ + ε₂)-transport when the distortion obeys a triangle inequality, with L the later kernel's stretch, so additive when that kernel is nonexpansive, as every Markov kernel is in total variation. Without a triangle inequality, or with an expansive kernel, the additive bound fails. | Answered |
| [QUESTION-294](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-294.md) | When a network's architecture can represent a structured system's renormalization step exactly, must training by distribution fitting make the variables it represents the system's relevant ones? | The representability part of [QUESTION-060](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-060.md), split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [THEORY-197](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-197.md) (Active) settles it, in the negative. Mehta and Schwab's RBM–renormalization correspondence is an identity of parametrizations, and an exact RG step is a perfect fit of the data distribution. Away from that point a contrastive-divergence RBM spends its hidden units on noise, not on the relevant fields. The architecture's match does not fix what training keeps. | Answered |
| [QUESTION-295](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-295.md) | Can processes that share one update rule and differ only in parameters and history come to hold stable, differentiated authority without any governance role being coded in, and can the same rule entrench whatever gained influence early? | The first part of [QUESTION-083](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-083.md), split off by the fourth status review under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [CLAIM-277](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-277.md), promoted on [CASE-182](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-182.md), settles it. | [QUESTION-296](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-296.md) | Can an intervention on what an interpreter is told about a communicative situation tell the relations that constitute the act from those that only accompany it? | The part of [QUESTION-030](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-030.md)'s empirical half that [CLAIM-130](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-130.md) settles, split off by the status review of 2026-10-28 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md). | [QUESTION-304](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-304.md) | Does acting as one require that an agent's interests synchronize? | The first side of [QUESTION-078](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-078.md), split off by the ninth status review under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) because [CLAIM-261](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-261.md) (Active) settles it: no. | [QUESTION-324](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-324.md) | Are the conditions an effective description is asked to meet (predictive sufficiency, dynamical independence, memory closure, approximation fidelity, tractability) of one logical kind, or are some of them parameters of the regime under which the others are assessed rather than conditions in their own right? | The last clause of [QUESTION-252](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-252.md), split off by the thirteenth status review under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) because [CLAIM-401](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-401.md) (Active) settles it: they are not of one kind. Predictive sufficiency and approximation fidelity are adequacy relative to a declared target, metric and horizon; tractability restricts the operations under which adequacy is assessed; dynamical independence and memory closure are relations of the representation to the system, memory relative to a chosen projection. Which conditions can fail while the others hold, and which configurations are impossible in which model classes, stays [QUESTION-252](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-252.md)'s. | Answered |
| [QUESTION-332](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-332.md) | Is the communicative object a presheaf over contexts? | The first remaining part of [QUESTION-055](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-055.md), split off by the fourteenth status review under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) because [CLAIM-038](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-038.md) (Active since 2026-10-29) settles it: a communicative object is a context-indexed system of empirical constraints over a cover of contexts, supports or distributions with their restrictions ([TERM-042](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-042.md)), which is a presheaf over contexts.
